title: Pipeline input and -WhatIf
summary: Functions that take objects from the pipeline (by value and by property name) with begin/process/end, and that support -WhatIf and -Confirm through SupportsShouldProcess.

steps.title: Taking input from the pipeline
body: A function can accept objects from `|` like any cmdlet. Mark the parameter, and put the work in a **`process`**
begin   { $now = Get-Date }                    # once, before the first object
end     { Write-Verbose 'done' }               # once, after the last object
- **`ValueFromPipeline`** binds the whole incoming object (here each `FileInfo`).
- **`ValueFromPipelineByPropertyName`** binds a **property with the same name** as the parameter (or one of its
`[Alias()]`es). That is what lets `Import-Csv users.csv | New-HomeFolder` fill `-UserName` and `-Department`
Without a `process` block, the body runs once at the **end**, with only the **last** object: the classic
"my function only handles one file" bug.

steps.explain: A body with no `begin`/`process`/`end` is treated as an `end` block: by then the parameter holds only the last object. `process` runs for each one.

steps.title: -WhatIf and -Confirm for your own functions
body: Anything that changes or deletes should support a dry run. Ask for it in `[CmdletBinding()]` and ask permission
- `$PSCmdlet.ShouldProcess(target, action)` returns `$false` and prints *What if: Performing the operation "Remove
old log" on target "..."* under `-WhatIf`, asks under `-Confirm`, and returns `$true` otherwise.
- `-WhatIf` also flows into the cmdlets you call (`Remove-Item` above), so nothing is missed.
- `ConfirmImpact = 'High'` makes PowerShell **ask by default** (because `$ConfirmPreference` is `High`); scripts then
pass `-Confirm:$false` deliberately. Keep it for truly dangerous operations (dropping a database).

steps.prompt: Put the skeleton of a pipeline function that supports -WhatIf in order.
steps.explain: `[CmdletBinding()]` comes before `param()`, and `ShouldProcess` is asked inside `process`, once per item, right before the change.

steps.title: Remove-OldLog with a dry run
prompt: - it takes **files from the pipeline** (`Get-ChildItem ~/logs/archive -File | Remove-OldLog`);
- **`-Days`** (default `30`): files whose `LastWriteTime` is older than that many days are deleted, the rest kept;
- **`-WhatIf`** shows what would go and deletes nothing; `-Confirm` asks per file.
Load it with `. ~/scripts/LogTools.ps1` and try it on `~/logs/archive` with `-WhatIf` first. The checks run it on

checks.name: -WhatIf deletes nothing and says what it would do
checks.cmd: d=$(mktemp -d); cp -a /opt/dojo/state/archive/. "$d"; out=$(pwsh -NoProfile -c ". ~/scripts/LogTools.ps1; Get-ChildItem $d -File | Remove-OldLog -WhatIf" 2>&1); echo "$out"; test "$(ls "$d" | wc -l)" = 5 && test "$(echo "$out" | grep -c 'What if')" = 3
checks.fail: With `-WhatIf` all five files must remain, and there should be three `What if:` lines (one per old file). Use `[CmdletBinding(SupportsShouldProcess)]` and `$PSCmdlet.ShouldProcess(...)`.

checks.name: the default of 30 days removes the three old files
checks.cmd: d=$(mktemp -d); cp -a /opt/dojo/state/archive/. "$d"; pwsh -NoProfile -c ". ~/scripts/LogTools.ps1; Get-ChildItem $d -File | Remove-OldLog" >/dev/null 2>&1; ls "$d" | tr '\n' ' '
checks.fail: Without `-Days`, files older than 30 days (`app-3.log`, `app-4.log`, `app-5.log`) should be deleted and the others kept. Is the work in a `process` block?

checks.name: -Days 10 removes more
checks.cmd: d=$(mktemp -d); cp -a /opt/dojo/state/archive/. "$d"; pwsh -NoProfile -c ". ~/scripts/LogTools.ps1; Get-ChildItem $d -File | Remove-OldLog -Days 10" >/dev/null 2>&1; ls "$d" | tr '\n' ' '
checks.fail: With `-Days 10`, only `app-1.log` (5 days old) should be left.

hints: Start from the skeleton in the lesson: `[CmdletBinding(SupportsShouldProcess)]`, then `param([Parameter(Mandatory, ValueFromPipeline)] [System.IO.FileInfo] $File, [int] $Days = 30)`.
Write the file with a here-string: `@' ... '@ | Set-Content ~/scripts/LogTools.ps1`, or `nano ~/scripts/LogTools.ps1`. Then `. ~/scripts/LogTools.ps1` to load it.
explain: `-Verbose` on a ShouldProcess function prints *Performing the operation ... on target ...* for every change it makes,
which is a free audit line in the job log. In module 5 this function moves into a module with tests that check

steps.prompt: A function declares `[CmdletBinding(SupportsShouldProcess, ConfirmImpact = 'High')]`. A scheduled task calls it without `-Confirm` or `-WhatIf`. What happens?
options: It asks for confirmation, and in a non-interactive session that fails, so nothing is changed
It behaves as if `-WhatIf` was given
steps.explain: `$ConfirmPreference` defaults to `High`, so operations of impact High prompt automatically. A scheduled caller must pass `-Confirm:$false` on purpose. That is the point: no accidental mass delete.

steps.title: Onboard new hires from a CSV
prompt: - `-UserName` and `-Department` come from the pipeline **by property name**, and both are mandatory;
- `-Department` must be one of `Engineering`, `Sales`, `Finance` (one row has `Marketing`: that row must fail with a
clear error **and the others must still be created**);
- `-Root` (default `~/homes`): it creates `<Root>/<Department>/<UserName>` and outputs the new folder;

checks.name: creates the four valid folders
checks.cmd: d=$(mktemp -d); pwsh -NoProfile -c ". ~/scripts/Onboarding.ps1; Import-Csv ~/data/new-hires.csv | New-HomeFolder -Root $d" >/dev/null 2>&1; (cd "$d" && find . -mindepth 2 -maxdepth 2 -type d | sort | tr '\n' ' ')
checks.fail: `Import-Csv ~/data/new-hires.csv | New-HomeFolder -Root <dir>` should create `<dir>/Engineering/asha.k`, `.../mira.s`, `Finance/tom.b` and `Sales/li.wen`, and nothing for Marketing.

checks.name: the Marketing row fails with a validation error
checks.cmd: d=$(mktemp -d); pwsh -NoProfile -c ". ~/scripts/Onboarding.ps1; Import-Csv ~/data/new-hires.csv | New-HomeFolder -Root $d" 2>&1 | grep -q 'does not belong to the set'
checks.fail: The `Marketing` row should be refused by `[ValidateSet('Engineering', 'Sales', 'Finance')]` on `-Department`.

checks.name: -WhatIf creates nothing
checks.fail: With `-WhatIf` the root folder must stay empty. `New-Item` inside a ShouldProcess function gets `-WhatIf` passed on automatically.

checks.name: outputs the new folders
checks.fail: The function should output one folder object per created home folder (four in total).

hints: `[Parameter(Mandatory, ValueFromPipelineByPropertyName)] [string] $UserName`, and the same for `$Department` plus a `[ValidateSet(...)]`.
In `process`: `$target = Join-Path $Root $Department $UserName`, then `if ($PSCmdlet.ShouldProcess($target, 'Create home folder')) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $target -Force }`.
explain: A validation failure on pipeline input is a **non-terminating** error for that one object: the bad row is reported
and the pipeline carries on with the next. In a real onboarding job, collect those errors (`-ErrorVariable failed`)
and send them back to HR instead of letting them scroll by.
